rows.text: Discarding is the resource here, not the cost. Doctor Doom drains the table every time you pitch a LAND, and the deck is built so that lands in hand are ammunition rather than dead cards. Then it wheels — and a wheel that makes you discard seven cards is seven separate triggers on the payoffs below. That is usually the game.

guide.title: The commander and the land engine

rows.name: Doctor Doom, King of Latveria
rows.text: every discard event that includes a land card drains each opponent for two, and every combat one of your Villains connives with menace — which is another discard, and another counter.

rows.name: Tectonic Reformation
rows.text: every land in your hand gains cycling {R}. Lands stop being flood and become "one mana: draw a card, drain the table for two." This is the card that makes the whole deck work.

rows.name: Trade Routes
rows.text: discard a land, draw a card, for {1} — and it can bounce your own lands back to hand to feed the engine again.

rows.name: Bone Miser
rows.text: discard a land and get {B}{B}; discard a spell and draw; discard a creature and make a 2/2. Every discard now pays for the next one.

rows.name: Crucible of Worlds
rows.text: play the lands back out of your graveyard. Between this and Trade Routes a single land can be discarded several times.

rows.name: Bazaar of Baghdad
rows.text: draw two, discard three, for free, every turn. In most decks that is unplayable; here it is three triggers a turn from a land.

rows.name: Surly Badgersaur
rows.text: a Treasure for every land you discard, a counter for every creature, and a fight for every spell.

rows.name: Green Goblin, Nemesis
rows.text: Treasures off land discards and counters off spell discards, on a flier.

rows.name: Monument to Endurance
rows.text: pick a different mode on each discard this turn — a card, a Treasure, or three life from each opponent. On a wheel turn it is all three.

rows.name: Wheel of Fortune
rows.text: everyone discards and draws seven. You are the only player at the table who is being paid for the discard half.

rows.name: Windfall
rows.text: the same effect, and it hits hardest when someone is hoarding.

rows.name: Dark Deal
rows.text: the mean one — they discard everything and draw one fewer. Cast it when your hand is nearly empty.

rows.name: Memory Jar
rows.text: seven new cards now, and everyone discards the new hand at end of turn. Two discard events for the price of one.

rows.name: Wheel of Misfortune
rows.text: name a number, deal that damage to whoever matched, and wheel everyone who did not choose the lowest. It doubles as reach.

rows.name: Waste Not
rows.text: the mirror of Bone Miser aimed at THEM. When your wheel makes three opponents discard seven cards each, you get Zombies, black mana and cards from twenty-one discards.

rows.name: Rielle, the Everwise
rows.text: the first time you discard each turn, draw that many. A Wheel of Fortune with Rielle out is seven cards, then seven more.

rows.name: Frantic Search
rows.text: free, draws two, discards two, and untaps three lands. It is a Doom trigger that costs nothing.

rows.name: Read the Runes
rows.text: draw X, then either discard X or sacrifice permanents. Both halves do something here.

rows.name: Glint-Horn Buccaneer
rows.text: one damage to EACH opponent per card discarded. A seven-card wheel is twenty-one damage spread across the table, and its own attacking ability turns every spare mana into another discard.

rows.name: Magmakin Artillerist
rows.text: damage to each opponent equal to the number of cards discarded at once. A wheel is seven to each player from a three-mana creature.

rows.name: Cool but Rude
rows.text: at level two, two damage to each opponent per discard. This is the highest-output payoff in the deck — level it up before you wheel.

rows.name: Archfiend of Ifnir
rows.text: every discard puts a -1/-1 counter on each of their creatures. A wheel is a board wipe that leaves your team untouched.

rows.name: Shadow of the Goblin
rows.text: a discard every upkeep for free, and it pings the table whenever you play something from outside your hand — which the exile-and-replay artifacts do constantly.

rows.name: Torment of Hailfire
rows.text: the finisher. After a wheel their hands are full but their boards are not, and every X is a real choice between life, a permanent and a card.

rows.name: Artist's Talent
rows.text: filters on every noncreature spell, then at level three adds two to all your noncombat damage — which upgrades every ping above.

guide.title: Playing the cards you threw away

rows.name: Containment Construct
rows.text: exile each discarded card and play it this turn. A wheel becomes "draw seven, and also play the seven you pitched."

rows.name: Moonstone, Harsh Mistress
rows.text: the same effect with a longer window — until the end of your NEXT turn — on a 2/4 flier.

rows.name: Currency Converter
rows.text: banks discarded cards, then cashes them in for Treasures and 2/2 bodies later.

rows.name: Chainer, Nightmare Adept
rows.text: discard a card to cast a creature out of your graveyard each turn, and anything you did not hard-cast gets haste.

rows.name: Master of Death
rows.text: surveils on entry and buys itself back from the graveyard every upkeep for one life. It is a free discard target forever.

rows.name: Psychic Frog
rows.text: a discard outlet that grows, draws on connection, and flies away when you need it to.

rows.name: Reanimate
rows.text: one mana for the biggest creature anyone has discarded, including the ones your wheel made THEM discard.

rows.name: Living Death
rows.text: after a wheel and a few turns of discards, your graveyard is deeper than theirs. Everyone sacrifices and everyone rebuilds — but you rebuild bigger.

rows.name: The Soul Stone
rows.text: once harnessed it returns a creature from your graveyard every single upkeep.

rows.name: Beseech the Mirror
rows.text: bargain it and cast the tutored card free if it costs four or less. Usually it fetches Wheel of Fortune, Torment of Hailfire or the missing payoff.

rows.name: Diabolic Intent
rows.text: turns a spare Zombie or Shapeshifter token into any card in the deck.

rows.name: Leader, Super-Genius
rows.text: upgrades every connive in the deck — you draw a card first, THEN the creature connives. It also connives something every combat on its own.

rows.name: Baron Strucker, HYDRA Overlord
rows.text: Villain spells cost one less, and every Villain that arrives connives.

rows.name: M.O.D.O.K.
rows.text: pay three life to connive at will, and every creature your opponents control is permanently -1/-1.

rows.name: Ledger Shredder
rows.text: connives on every player's second spell each turn, so a wheel turn grows it and filters for you at the same time.

rows.name: Green Goblin, Revenant
rows.text: discards on attack, then draws for EVERY card you have discarded that turn. After a wheel it refills your hand by itself.

rows.name: Moonstone, Harsh Mistress
rows.text: also a Villain, so Doom's combat trigger can point at her.

rows.name: Rhystic Study
rows.text: nobody pays the one when you are the player forcing them to spend mana on their own turn.

rows.name: Mystic Remora
rows.text: the early-game version, best on turns one through four.

rows.name: Black Market Connections
rows.text: three modes a turn for life, and the Treasures pay for the cycling costs.

rows.name: Orcish Bowmasters
rows.text: every wheel makes each opponent draw seven, so Bowmasters triggers eighteen times off one Wheel of Fortune. Play it BEFORE you wheel.

rows.name: Mana Drain
rows.text: counters the answer and pays for Torment of Hailfire next turn.

rows.name: Force of Negation
rows.text: free protection for your combo turn on their turn.

rows.name: Fierce Guardianship
rows.text: the same, with your commander out.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: redirects the removal or the counterspell aimed at your engine.

rows.name: Muddle the Mixture
rows.text: a counterspell, or transmute for Rhystic Study, Bone Miser, Waste Not or Monument to Endurance.

rows.name: Deadly Rollick
rows.text: free exile for the creature that is about to kill you.

rows.name: Toxic Deluge
rows.text: scalable wrath that gets under indestructible.

rows.name: Withering Torment
rows.text: creature or enchantment, at instant speed.

rows.name: Chaos Warp
rows.text: the only clean answer to an enchantment or planeswalker in these colours.

rows.name: Vandalblast
rows.text: overloaded, it wipes the table's artifacts and leaves yours alone.

rows.name: Rakdos Charm
rows.text: graveyard hate, artifact removal, or a symmetric ping that finishes a token board.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep lands. Genuinely — this is one of the few decks where a seven-card hand with six lands is fine, because Tectonic Reformation, Trade Routes and Bazaar of Baghdad turn every one of them into a card and two life from each opponent.

Get a payoff down before you wheel. Wheel of Fortune with an empty board is a card-neutral shuffle; Wheel of Fortune with Glint-Horn Buccaneer, Cool but Rude or Orcish Bowmasters out is often twenty damage spread across the table.

rows.name: Doctor Doom, King of Latveria
rows.text: four mana, and he does not need to be first. The engine pieces — Tectonic Reformation, Bone Miser, Monument to Endurance — are what make him lethal, so deploy those and cast him into a turn where you can immediately discard.

rows.name: Cool but Rude
rows.text: level it to two before you wheel, not after. The difference between level one and level two on a seven-card wheel is fourteen damage to each opponent.
